The '''1963 [[German football championship]]''' was the culmination of the [[football (soccer)|football]] season in the [[West Germany|Federal Republic of Germany]] in [[1962–63 Oberliga|1962–63]]. [[Borussia Dortmund]] were crowned champions for the third time after a group stage and a final, having previously won the championship in [[1956 German football championship|1956]] and [[1957 German football championship|1957]].<ref>[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html (West) Germany -List of champions] rsssf.org, accessed: 22 December 2015</ref>

Defending champions [[1. FC Köln]] made its third appearance in the final, having won the previous year's championship and lost in [[1960 German football championship|1960]], but lost 3-1 to Borussia Dortmund.

On the strength of this title, Borussia Dortmund participated in the [[1963–64 European Cup]], where the team lost to [[Inter Milan]] in the semi-finals.

The format used to determine the German champion was similar to the one used in the 1962 season. Nine clubs qualified for the tournament, with the runners-up of the South and the North having to play a qualifying match. The remaining eight clubs then played a home-and-away round in two groups of four, with the two group winners entering the final. In the previous year, a single round had been played in the group stages because of the [[1962 FIFA World Cup]], in order to reduce the schedule and not hinder [[Germany national football team|West Germany]] at the tournament in Chile, where West Germany was knocked out by [[Yugoslavia national football team|Yugoslavia]] in the quarterfinals.

The 1963 edition was the last edition before the introduction of the [[Bundesliga]], and the last one to have a championship final match. From 1963-64 onwards, the German championship would have a consistent format with 18 teams and 34 matches, in a double round-robin tournament (except in 1991-92, when due to [[German reunification]] the league had 20 teams and 38 matches).
